candidates.decision_relevance: Would replace the repeatedly invalid or shortened nominal 1-hour, 4-hour, 12-hour, 24-hour, and 72-hour windows with timestamped observations having known actual spans, reducing horizon and recency ambiguity in pullback and transmission analyses.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly report unavailable 1-hour anchors, zero-span 4-hour records, and actual spans materially shorter than nominal horizons.
candidates.metric_name: Validated hourly BTC/ETH/ETH-BTC price sequence with anchor timestamps
candidates.missing_history_problem: The analyses cannot distinguish genuine multi-horizon sequencing from irregular or overlapping capture-to-capture changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would establish whether breadth deterioration or recovery persisted rather than reflecting endpoint selection or changing constituent membership.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly and daily reviews identify single-endpoint breadth, missing breadth paths, and differing membership hashes between captures.
candidates.metric_name: Fixed-universe constituent breadth and return panel
candidates.missing_history_problem: Breadth changes are not reliably comparable across captures and cannot support persistence or breadth-survival assessment.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would make leverage-stress interpretation comparable across the same price windows and reveal whether OI-price divergence persisted across assets and venues.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly describe OI as mixed or horizon-dependent and lack underlying series, venue coverage, and comparable history.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped venue-normalized BTC/ETH open-interest and price-change series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Point-to-point OI changes cannot distinguish persistent leverage behavior from venue, horizon, or capture-timing differences.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would test whether unchanged or rising funding was persistent and whether funding conditions preceded subsequent price outcomes.
candidates.evidence_reference: Multiple analyses cite funding as unchanged or modest but lack a complete comparable funding history.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped BTC/ETH funding-rate history by venue
candidates.missing_history_problem: The framework cannot assess funding persistence, acceleration, or lead-lag behavior rather than relying on isolated snapshots.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would materially improve evaluation of the rotation and transmission analyses by supplying the absent market-wide participation and dominance context.
candidates.evidence_reference: Rotation hypotheses repeatedly cannot be evaluated because BTC dominance, Total2, Total3, and stablecoin dominance changes are missing.
candidates.metric_name: BTC dominance, Total2, Total3, and stablecoin-dominance history
candidates.missing_history_problem: ETH/BTC and breadth observations cannot be separated from broad market-cap rotation or stablecoin-share changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would determine whether the isolated positive settled ETF observations represented persistent flows or a one-session artifact when assessing transmission.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly state that ETF context is limited to one settled session and lacks a comparable change series.
candidates.metric_name: Settled daily BTC and ETH ETF flow history
candidates.missing_history_problem: ETF evidence cannot support a time-series transmission or persistence assessment.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would allow the current option measure to be evaluated against its own historical distribution and price outcomes instead of being treated as an isolated, non-25-delta snapshot.
candidates.evidence_reference: Analyses repeatedly note that moneyness-bucket skew lacks equivalent historical snapshots and is not 25-delta skew.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped option-chain moneyness-bucket skew history with expiry metadata
candidates.missing_history_problem: The observed skew cannot be classified as unusual, persistent, or historically associated with subsequent moves.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would clarify whether liquidation-based stress observations were complete and whether acceleration persisted across venues and windows.
candidates.evidence_reference: Liquidation evidence is repeatedly described as lower-bound, potentially truncated, and of unverified completeness.
candidates.metric_name: Complete timestamped liquidation event stream with venue and pagination coverage
candidates.missing_history_problem: Aggregate liquidation counts and notionals may be understated or selectively sampled, weakening leverage-stress interpretation.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would provide the missing contemporaneous macro context for separating crypto-specific pullbacks from broader liquidity or risk-factor moves.
candidates.evidence_reference: Macro/FRED observations are repeatedly unavailable because the macro owner is disabled.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped macro and financial-condition observations used by the existing analyses
candidates.missing_history_problem: The analyses cannot evaluate whether observed crypto weakness or strength coincided with changing macro conditions.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would enable actual prospective validation of the repeatedly unratified directional and range candidates, including containment and timing outcomes.
candidates.evidence_reference: The weekly review states that candidate definitions and matured outcomes are absent, leaving false-positive, false-negative, containment, and opportunity-cost assessment unavailable.
candidates.metric_name: Archived candidate specifications, formation timestamps, and matured outcome records
candidates.missing_history_problem: Descriptive fit cannot be distinguished from prospective forecasting skill, and range precision cannot be assessed.
